instruction: gin handlers cannot report failures except by writing a response or calling `c.Error` themselves. Change the handler type in gin.go from `type HandlerFunc func(*Context)` to `type HandlerFunc func(*Context) error`, and make `Context.Next` record a handler's non-nil error with `c.Error(err)` (appending it to `c.Errors`) before moving on to the next handler, exactly as if the handler had called `c.Error(err)` itself; a nil error changes nothing. Every handler in the module must then return an `error`: handler function literals (route handlers, middleware such as the closures returned by `Logger`/`LoggerWithConfig`, `Recovery`/`CustomRecoveryWithWriter`, `BasicAuthForRealm`, `ErrorLoggerT`, `WrapF`/`WrapH`, ...), named handler functions, and every handler in tests and in the `ginS` and `binding`/`render`/other subpackages. Existing handlers never fail: each returns `nil` -- every bare `return` in a handler's own body becomes `return nil` and a body that falls off the end gets a final `return nil` -- while `return` statements inside other func literals nested in a handler (stream callbacks, goroutines, deferred funcs) stay as they are. Do not add an adapter type or a wrapper that converts old-style `func(*Context)` handlers, and do not change `RecoveryFunc`, `HandlersChain` or the router's registration methods beyond what the new `HandlerFunc` type implies. Behavior must not change.
gold_tool: build_deep.py deephard go recipe: type + Next by pattern; handler funcs located from go build/go test compile errors (-gcflags=-e, default and nomsgpack tags) and rewritten with go/ast positions (deephard_astq.go: own returns only, nested func literals excluded), iterated to a clean build; gofmt (go1.25 GOTOOLCHAIN=local)
change: change a func type's result (HandlerFunc gains an error result): every handler literal, named handler and middleware closure returns error; bare returns in their own bodies become `return nil`, nested func literals untouched; Next records the error
notes: Handler bodies vary: early bare returns, nested func literals with their own returns (c.Stream callbacks, goroutines, defers), panicking bodies, one-line literals, named handlers shared by several tests, closures returned by middleware factories.
